entries.subject: Margoti et al. (2026) three-dimensional oblate fit
entries.finding: The selected shape is the published oblate fit to 36 stellar-occultation campaigns, with equatorial semiaxes 566.1 km and polar semiaxis 511.2 km, using the ring plane as a pole constraint; the source survey was checked on 2026-09-09.

entries.subject: Ring-plane pole prior
entries.finding: The display pole at right ascension 259.7 degrees and declination 53.4 degrees inherits the measured ring-plane prior; the meridian is arbitrary.

entries.subject: Pereira et al. (2023) ring radii
entries.finding: The two ring radii, Q1R at 4057.2 km and Q2R at 2520 km, come from this publication; Q1R is drawn with the 76.4 km width of the tenuous component measured at one Gemini chord and Q2R with the published typical 10 km width.

entries.subject: Schematic ring bands
entries.finding: Both bands use the shared terrestrial ring preparation capability as uniform circular schematics; the dense arc is not reconstructed and the uniform gray and display opacity are illustrative, not measured reflectance or optical depth.

entries.subject: Competing triaxial shape and spin-period interpretations
entries.finding: The README records that oblate versus triaxial shape remains unresolved, that the pole assumes alignment with the rings, and that the 8.8394-hour and 17.6788-hour spin interpretations are model-dependent, so neither is installed as a sidereal spin.
entries.revisitWhen: A new occultation campaign or an independent pole determination decides the shape, or a secure sidereal period is published.

entries.subject: 572.5 MB supplementary archive of lightcurves and model profiles
entries.finding: The source survey records that the archive holds lightcurves and model profiles rather than a resolved surface texture, and that it was not downloaded for the published numeric fit.
entries.revisitWhen: The archive or a successor release is shown to contain a resolved surface product.

entries.subject: cssEarth missing-coverage grid as the surface
entries.finding: Surface detail is unresolved, so the manifest supplies the project-authored missing-data grid to mark unmapped terrain, with Shadows off by default and no reconstruction from surface spectra.
